usage: This is the standard, everyday greeting used from late afternoon until the end of the night. It is appropriate for all formalities and social situations across the Levant, and the base phrase does not change based on the gender or number of people being addressed.

variants.label: standard
variants.note: The default greeting for any situation.

variants.label: warm alternative (to a man)
variants.note: A very common and slightly more affectionate alternative used when addressing a male.

variants.label: warm alternative (to a woman)
variants.note: The feminine equivalent of the warm alternative.

variants.label: warm alternative (to a group)
variants.note: Used when addressing two or more people.

variants.label: plural/enthusiastic
variants.note: A cheerful, pluralized version often used when entering a room full of people.

examples.arabic: مَسَا الخَيْر يَا شَبَاب، كِيفكُم اليُوم؟
examples.transliteration: masa l-kheir ya shabab, kifkom l-yom?
examples.english: Good evening guys, how are you today?
Good evening, is there a table for two?
Good evening to you all, please come in and make yourselves comfortable.
